headline: Jeff Bezos has predicted that AI could let some people support a family on a three-day workweek, while Amazon has cut about 30,000 corporate jobs since late 2025.
score_reason: Lowered by one: the interview aired on 7 Oct 2026, before the window, and the forecast is a personal view with no numbers behind it.
importance_line: Workers hear a promise of shorter weeks from the head of a company that has cut many jobs, but Bezos gave no timeline or plan for how AI gains would reach employees rather than owners, so it remains an opinion.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports on a Fox News interview aired on 7 Oct 2026 in which Amazon founder Jeff Bezos said AI-driven productivity gains could let some workers support a family on three days a week, and anchor Bret Baier questioned him about Amazon's roughly 30,000 corporate job cuts since late 2025. Bezos presented the forecast as his own vision and blamed the cuts mainly on pandemic-era overhiring, but gave no timeline or calculation for how gains would reach workers.
notes: Source credited to the Fox News interview; text read in the Yahoo Finance article, which comments on it.
